title: Execution, Realization, Effect and Consequence
results: Dispatch, start, execution, realization, effect, consequence and outcome are distinct semantic layers.
Execution is best modeled as contract-governed realization behavior under a named execution envelope rather than process existence alone.
Multiple nested execution envelopes can coexist and execution-start claims must name scope where ambiguity matters.
Environment/setup realization can precede target execution.
Current DISPATCH_ISSUED is a durable at-most-once dispatch commitment/issue boundary before provider submission rather than start proof.
Realization is a specification/commitment-to-concrete-behavior relation broader than Job/Runner execution.
Realization lineage preserves identity-bound participation evidence without asserting exclusive causal ownership.
Effect is a contract-relevant external-world change relative to a declared projection and effect owner.
Requested effect, actual effect, incidental effect, consequence and semantic outcome remain distinct.
Effect occurrence is distinct from effect-condition or operation-semantic satisfaction, allowing idempotent no-op success without inventing a new mutation.
Provider acceptance, transport result and local execution terminality do not by themselves determine external effect completion.
Receipt is identity-bound scoped evidence rather than the effect itself.
Effects can precede local execution failure or occur asynchronously after client execution terminates.
Atomic visibility, durability and finality are distinct effect properties.
Cancellation and timeout are execution-control facts and do not imply external rollback or effect failure.
Runtime self-release and Workspace Patch confirm that effect-specific receipts and reconciliation can outrank generic process inference.
Workspace Patch proves structured effect realization does not require Job/Runner execution and that receipt loss can be reconciled without replaying a mixed effect.
Current Ordivon Runtime generically owns committed-operation realization lineage and execution evidence, with external effect truth only under structured effect/domain contracts.
